granularity_problems.issue: f2 glues two sequential but independently meaningful steps into one fact: (a) tweets were filtered using the possible names referring to the target clubs, and (b) the stance of the filtered tweets was then annotated as Favor or Against. A reader could lose the filtering-method detail and still have the core annotation answer (Favor/Against), or vice versa, so per the protocol's own splitting test these read as two facts, not one ('firstly filtered... Then, we have annotated...' marks a clear procedural break, not a single bundled cause/rationale like the retry-loop example in the protocol).

notes: Coverage against the three native-evidence paragraphs is otherwise complete and well-grounded: all five source_quotes verified verbatim, background/motivation sentences and future-work commentary are correctly excluded as out of scope for 'how were the tweets annotated', and no relation is missing since the facts function as independent descriptive/constraint statements rather than connective claims.
